claims.name: Choir - The Choir was an area furnished with stalls where the religious community gathered for services. These were recited or chanted throughout the day. The Abbey of St. Mary was founded for Augustinian canons in around 1124 and closed by Henry VIII in 1538. Although by 1600 most of the building had been dismantled some parts survive today both above and below ground. The name 'Abbey Fields' reminds us of the Abbey that once stood here.

claims.name: Chapter House - The canons met daily in the chapter house. They listened to reading from the rule of St. Augustine, confessed their sins and were disciplined by the Abbot. Although by 1600 most of the building had been dismantled some parts survive today both above and below ground. The name 'Abbey Fields' reminds us of the Abbey that once stood here.

claims.name: Dormitory - The canons slept in the Dorter (dormitory) , a long room with beds arranged each side. Latrines (lavatories) with drains flushed by water were sited at the south end of this building. The Abbey of St. Mary was founded for Augustinian canons in around 1124 and closed by Henry VIII in 1538. Although by 1600 most of the building had been dismantled some parts survive today both above and below ground. The name 'Abbey Fields' reminds us of the Abbey that once stood here.

claims.name: Nave - The nave was used by the public until St. Nicholas’ Church was built nearby sometime before 1291. The nave continued to be used  by the lay brothers for non-religious activities.
